newsitem.title: USA: USTR outlines global trade barriers in report.
newsitem.headline: USTR outlines global trade barriers in report.

text.p: The U.S. Trade Representative's Office on Monday released a 381-page report providing a country-by-country breakdown of trade barriers that it says thwart U.S. sales abroad.
Some 45 pages of the report are devoted to Japan, where the USTR said problems involving a number of business sectors remain despite 24 trade agreements since 1992.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in a statement accompanying the report specifically pointed to problems concerning Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).

"Despite recent progress with procurement among some Japanese government agencies, I am particularly concerned that the results U.S. companies have achieved with NTT compared with the private Japanese telecommunications sector suggests NTT is still captive to its monopoly legacy and not fully responsive to market principles," she said.
The USTR devoted some 35 pages to the European Union, which it said maintains barriers to U.S. exports in many key areas.

"I am particularly concerned by the EU's pervasive discrimination against U.S. agricultural exports -- including rice, wheat, wheat flour, bananas, beef, dairy products and certain fruit," Barshefsky said.
"We have been working aggressively on all these issues to ensure the EU's full compliance with its internaitonal commitments to provide fair access to U.S. agricultural products," she said.
